item.title: Keeping Humans in the Loop in the AI-Driven Future of Information Security
item.content:encoded:
Laura Amo, University at Buffalo, State University of New York

Richard Baskerville, Georgia State University

Rui Chen, Iowa State University

Matthew Hashim, University of Arizona

Yaojie (William) Li, University of New Orleans

Yuan Li, University of Tennessee at Knoxville

As artificial intelligence increasingly dominates both offensive and defensive cybersecurity, this special issue emphasizes maintaining human involvement in security systems and decision-making. While AI tools help detect threats and respond to attacks, they introduce new risks through generative AI-enabled phishing and behavioral manipulation. The issue seeks research balancing AI's role with human judgment and responsibility in information security.

Papers should explore how design science approaches create intelligent security artifacts enhancing human decision-making rather than replacing it, and how to mitigate human vulnerabilities while leveraging human strengths in AI-mediated security. Both established behavioral security topics and emerging issues related to AI risks and secure behavior in modern work environments are welcome.

Appel publié par Information Systems Frontiers. Voir l'appel sur le site de l'éditeur. Fiche de l'appel sur kerostig.

Potential topics

  • Neurosecurity (NeuroIS) investigations of information security behavior
  • Design science treatments balancing security and privacy tradeoffs
  • Cybersecurity/privacy and AI/ML advancements intersection
  • AI-enabled security awareness, training, nudging, and behavioral interventions
  • Human-AI collaboration in security decision-making and response
  • Generative AI behavioral security implications: phishing, social engineering, insider threats
  • Intelligent security artifacts with behavioral implications
  • Adaptive and context-aware security interventions enabled by AI
  • Behavioral security theories in AI-mediated environments
  • Security behaviors in remote work, hybrid work, IoT, and cloud environments
